gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads in a high-set midline, its counters staying linked to the outside. Nippo is the showman, with small letters standing nearly capital-tall in wire-cut strokes, while the plain sans body does the quieter work of keeping text open and easy to follow.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Nippo's lowercase stands almost as tall as its capitals, with strokes that look like bent copper pipe. Noto Sans Thaana follows with wide channels into big open forms.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai swells its lowercase like inflated glass beads, leaving the rounded letters open. Nippo, by contrast, draws lines of essentially zero contrast and gives headings a wiry, technical edge, and the body keeps the plumpness.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall bodies that make its lowercase look bold. If Nippo were made small, its uniform wire-like line would lose its punch, while the sans-serif body keeps its spacious curve terminals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Nippo draws a lowercase a with no thin hairlines, cut like wire. Noto Sans Tifinagh fills the line with rounded, inviting bowls, so one brings the technical sharpness and the other the open, inflated shapes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Nippo's strokes look like cut ribbon of constant width. Noto Sans Tirhuta has terminals cut back to leave a big gap and a dominant x-height, which makes the two feel like crisp, modern cousins.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Wiry, compact and nearly all capitals in feel. Nippo replaces hairline joins with full-width connections, and Noto Sans Ugaritic matches that closeness with little gap between x-height and cap height, its open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-vai: Nippo's t has a crossbar and stem sharing one width. Noto Sans Vai makes words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space where curves meet stems, so text moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Nippo holds each stroke at one thickness, like drawn cable. Noto Sans Vithkuqi does the opposite kind of job, with open throats on a, c, e and s and a minimal step from capital to lowercase for smooth sans text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Technical and contemporary, Nippo draws its line at constant width like a marker. Noto Sans Wancho is the heavy one, a hulking lowercase like thick chalk pressed hard, with an e that gapes wide at the terminal.
